key_insight: Intern-Atlas transforms paper-centric citation networks into a machine-readable Methodological Evolution Graph that explicitly encodes how AI methods emerge, adapt, and build on one another, enabling reliable reasoning by human researchers and AI agents.
problem_solved: Current research infrastructure is document-centric and lacks structured representations of methodological lineage, so researchers and AI agents cannot easily trace provenance, composition, or the evolutionary relationships between methods.
method: Represent methods as rich nodes (metadata: implementation, hyperparameters, datasets, performance, code/artifacts) and encode directed edges for derivation/adaptation/augmentation relationships.
Automatically infer relationships by combining citation parsing, code/repo linkage, artifact/version tracking, and semantic analysis of method descriptions.
Expose the graph via a machine-readable schema, APIs, and visualization tools to support querying, agent consumption, and reproducible method retrieval.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners and research agents with a structured, queryable map of methodological progress — improving discoverability, reproducibility, and the ability to transfer or combine methods efficiently.
visual_elements: Methodological Evolution Graph: nodes = methods, colored by family; directed edges show derivation/adaptation paths.
Timeline/flowchart showing key branches and forks in a method family (e.g., baseline → modification → ensemble).
Node detail card mockup with metadata: paper, code link, key hyperparameters, benchmark results, and provenance breadcrumbs.
Example agent workflow diagram: natural-language query → graph traversal → recommended methods + reproducible setup.
paper_title: Intern-Atlas: A Methodological Evolution Graph as Research Infrastructure for AI Scientists
paper_authors: Yujun Wu, Dongxu Zhang, Xinchen Li, Jinhang Xu, Yiling Duan
